chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Kūfī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “The grave-robber and the pickpocket have their hand cut off, but the snatcher does not have his hand cut off.”
ʿAlī, from his father, from Ādam ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī, who said:

I was with Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام when a letter from Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to him concerning a man who had dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and had intercourse with her. The people had differed here about him: one group said, “Kill him,” and another group said, “Burn him.”

So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام wrote back to him: “The sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living. His prescribed punishment is that his hand be cut off for grave-digging and taking the clothes, and that the prescribed punishment for zina be carried out upon him: if he was muḥṣan, he is stoned; and if he was not muḥṣan, he is flogged one hundred lashes.”

key_terms.أُحْصِنَ: being legally muḥṣan, meaning previously married in a way relevant to the hadd ruling
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse subject to hadd punishment
key_terms.الطَّرَّارُ: the pickpocket who stealthily takes property
key_terms.النَّبَّاشُ: the one who digs up graves in order to steal from the dead
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِسُ: the snatcher who seizes property openly and quickly without meeting the legal threshold for amputation here
key_terms.جُلِدَ مِائَةً: he is flogged one hundred lashes
key_terms.حُرْمَةَ الْمَيِّتِ: the inviolable sanctity of the deceased person
key_terms.رُجِمَ: he is stoned as the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on grave robbery, pickpocketing, and violating the sanctity of the dead in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning theft-related crimes and violation of graves, distinguishing between cases that incur amputation and those that do not. It also affirms that the sanctity of a deceased person is equal to that of the living, and applies hadd punishments accordingly in cases involving grave desecration and zina.
